data.long_meaning: In Persian culture, Homadokht is the name given to the goddess of fertility, abundance, and prosperity. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. data.cultural_impact: In ancient Iranian mythology, Homadokht, also known as Anahita, was a major goddess revered for her role as the goddess of water, fertility, abundance, and prosperity. Her cult spread from northwestern Iran into central Asia, Anatolia, Syria, and Egypt. In Persian art and literature, she is often depicted wearing a diadem, seated on a throne, holding a cornucopia and year, or accompanied by a snake or lotus. Her festival, Anahit-Mas, was celebrated in midwinter, the time of harvest, in honor of her power to bless the land with a bountiful crop.
data.spiritual_significance: Homadokht's name reflects her role as a giver of life and prosperity, a nurturing and protective mother figure. She is believed to be the guardian of fertility, a bringer of abundance and prosperity, and a source of comfort and solace. In spiritually exploring the name Homadokht, one might reflect on the idea of abundance and fertility, not just in terms of physical resources and children, but in all aspects of life, including personal growth, creativity, and relationships. One might also seek inner peace, comfort, and connection to the natural world, as Homadokht is often associated with water, which symbolizes the flow of life and the interconnectedness of all things.
